editor_notes: The 12 must takes total 66 s against the 45 s target and 67.5 s cap. The script alone times at 49 s, so the reference assembly cannot preserve every scripted duration and also reach 45 s without compression; do not trim dialogue to force the target.

Timing remains at risk: the checker estimates 4B-1 needs 8.6 s for an 8 s take; 4A-2 needs 6.1 s for 6 s; 4C-1 needs 6.4 s for 6 s; 4F-2 needs 5.7 s for 4 s; and 4A-4 needs 6.1 s for 6 s. These are not cleared by the check. Verify full performances and pauses before conform; if they do not fit, request a cap revision or additional overlapping coverage in the cinematic pass rather than truncate a line. There is only 1.5 s of cap headroom, less than the smallest additional take.

Use 4A-1 for the right-hand phone transfer, 4B-1 and the shared dialogue frames for the growing connection, 4E-1 to establish the ringing source and caller ID, 4F-1 to connect the call, 4F-2 and 4G-1 for the remote line and its effect, 4A-3 to return to their shared space, and 4H-1 for the separation.

L8 and L9 change setup and size at their sentence boundary. L13–L15 are remote audio, never lip-performed; cut to the tighter listening angle at the sentence boundary before L15. Retain complete audio and never invent knowledge for Kasun.

Keep the same axis, wardrobe, prop hands, open umbrella, rain and daylight. The phone begins with Kasun in the handover despite the coarse opening state listing it with Anudi. Her handbag stays on her left forearm and umbrella in her left hand; she takes the phone with her right. Anudi is already oriented toward her departure at the final cut.
On the phone screen, Father is the chosen English contact label; the script specifies identity but not the exact label. Confirm the production's preferred label before generation.

For silent-picture takes 4A-1 and 4H-1, add the planned rain, traffic and footsteps in the sound mix rather than letting Veo invent voices. The phone ring begins only after the incoming display is visible.

No ornamental match transition is required; preserve eyelines and match the right-hand phone position across cuts. Any speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in or split screen is post-only and would require a clean source; none is prescribed for this grounded scene.
Avoid mirrors, split diopters, fast finger choreography and contact between bodies. One simple screen touch connects or ends each call.
